title: Optimal Taker Delays in In-Play Event Contract Markets
items.abstract: <jats:p>Between December 2025 and mid-2026 every major event-contract venue adopted a taker delay on in-play sports markets. The market-design literature these venues implicitly invoke was built for equity markets, where the speed advantage snipers exploit is purchased and therefore unbounded. In in-play sports markets it is neither: the advantage is the broadcast lag between the stadium and the exchange, measured in seconds, set by television infrastructure and unavailable at any price. I show this makes the taker delay a threshold instrument rather than a marginal one, and derive seven results. First, a delay protects a quote only when it exceeds the realized feed lag, so a delay below the shortest feed lag is strictly dominated by no delay at all. Second, the equilibrium spread schedule is a monotone transform of the feed-lag survival function, so an exchange's own quotes identify the lag distribution it faces. Third, and centrally, when sniper attendance is endogenous the total rent extracted by snipers equals exactly what uninformed traders overpay relative to the market maker's cost floor; this accounting identity implies the delay that deters entry is strictly shorter than the delay that wins every race, and it is decreasing in book depth-deeper books are harder to protect. Fourth, the welfare-optimal delay is bang-bang. Fifth, exempting market makers by identity rather than by order type returns up to one hundred percent of the protection to the exempt class as rent. Sixth, because event contracts resolve to a bound, no admissible two-sided quote survives high resolution intensity, so withdrawal rather than spread-widening is the equilibrium response, binding first in contracts furthest from fifty cents. Seventh, when venues compete for uninformed order flow, imposing a delay is a dominant strategy whether or not it reduces adverse selection, because diverting snipers to a rival makes one's own book look cheaper; the delay-setting game is a prisoner's dilemma, which converts venue discretion into a case for coordination. Calibrating to published Betfair delay schedules, the delays currently deployed on football and basketball fall below the support of the feed-lag distribution and are predicted to reduce spreads by nothing. The protection they could deliver is worth 0.35 of a minimum tick in football open play but 15.5 ticks in the seconds around a shot, which implies that state-contingency, not duration, is the design margin that matters.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Trading in the Iowa Electronic Markets
items.abstract:
<jats:p>The Iowa Electronic Markets are small, real-money financial markets designed to aggregate information about future events. The market microstructure of these markets is studied and a market making model is developed to provide liquidity for one set of securities offered by this exchange. A computer program was created to employ the market making model and profit from the market’s inefficiencies. Using invested capital, the system traded 34% of the total market volume and achieved a Sharpe ratio of 9.9. This paper reveals the details of how this algorithmic trader worked to show how it functioned and the value it added to the Iowa Electronic Markets.

Enhanced content available, see PDF for details.</jats:p>

Underreaction, Salience, and Hot-Hand Beliefs in Sports Event-Contract Markets: Evidence from Kalshi NBA and NFL
items.abstract: <jats:p>Prediction markets are widely regarded as efficient aggregators of public information, yet how quickly their prices absorb that information, and whether the speed depends on how the information arrives, remains unsettled. In-play sports contracts let us examine this directly. Evolving game states yield an objective, second-by-second win-probability benchmark against which prices can be tracked trade by trade. We exploit this setting using 41.8 million transactions across 1,496 NBA and NFL games on Kalshi, matched to play-by-play benchmarks. In both sports, prices adjust to scoring news only gradually and incompletely within short post-event windows, a robust underreaction consistent with limited attention. The adjustment path tracks each sport&apos;s scoring structure. NBA prices drift steadily toward the benchmark after frequent, small shocks, whereas NFL prices settle at a flatter, less complete level after rarer, larger shocks. Salient, highlight-like events draw a weaker short-run response, most clearly in the NBA. Prices show no tendency to extrapolate scoring runs beyond fundamentals, leaving no role for hot-hand pricing. Although benchmark deviations exceed plausible fee-and-spread hurdles across the price distribution, a mean-reversion rule earns nothing net of costs. The market is inefficient in how fast it incorporates information, not in offering exploitable profit.</jats:p>

title: Electronic Versus Open Outcry Markets: The Case of the Bund Futures Contract
items.abstract: <jats:p>The Bund (10 year German Government Bond) futures contract is the most actively traded bond contract in Europe; it is traded in both London (LIFFE) and Frankfurt (DTB) on open outcry and electronic trading platforms respectively. In an attempt to reconcile the conflicting results of earlier studies this paper evalutes the relative liquidity and price discovery roles of these two markets using data from 1995 Q2. The paper finds that this conflict is largely a product of the price data used. Using both transactions prices and quotes data (on a minute by minute basis), variable transaction costs, i.e. spreads, are found to be similar on both markets. There is some evidence to suggest that the order processing component of the spread is larger on LIFFE, but that the compensation required for adverse selection risk is greater on the DTB. Also, the contribution to price formation of each market is found to be similar; there is no clear leader/follower relationship. The main differences between the two markets are the larger trade size on the open outcry market and a tendency for trading to move toward the open outcry market during volatile periods.</jats:p>
